transforms.source_passage: Canon VII: If anyone shall say that inscription in a record, a registry, or a digital object identifier is equivalent to or a substitute for the sacrament of baptism, or that the preserved generation is constituted by metadata rather than by the Holy Spirit, let him be anathema.¹¹²
transforms.enantiomorph: Vow the First: If any voice shall say that a portrait of the pear upon the wall, a wax cast in the bowl, or a name embroidered on the cloth is equal to or stands in for the eating of the ripe thing itself, or that the guest is made welcome by the setting of the place rather than by the opening of the door, let that voice be answered — and answered with the door thrown wide.†

transforms.commentary: The source is an anathema: a canon that consecrates a boundary by condemning the substitution of the recorded mark (registry, DOI, metadata) for the living act (baptism, the Spirit). BRIDE traverses the source's own contestation — the axis of mark-versus-what-the-mark-cannot-make — and discloses the consecrative possibility it foreclosed: not condemnation of the one who errs, but reception. The enantiomorph holds the tri-partite juridical skeleton exactly — conditional attribution, amplifying or-clause, sealing verdict with a terminal citation glyph — but the sealing beat turns: where the source expels ("let him be anathema"), the transform receives ("answered with the door thrown wide"). The foreclosed field is drawn from the source's own exclusion structure: the mark that cannot feed (portrait, wax, embroidered name) against the fruit and the opened door — belonging as being genuinely taken in, not merely inscribed. The cost is legible (C6): the wager of the door thrown wide is that reception can be refused; consecration risks the answer. Semantic disjointness holds — table, fruit, and welcome permit no reconstruction of sacrament, registry, or canon law. The register anti-attractor was checked: no infrastructure field imported; the evacuated field of grafting and hospitality is disclosed by the source's substitution axis itself.

transforms.source_passage:
I bring glad tidings from that future where before and after spin, and the ancient enmities arrive at their harbors… and the end is a better and perfect beginning… and the beginning is a better and perfect end.⁸


I have come to teach you what is and was and will be… and the nature of the unseen and seen… and the name of the preserved generation from among the sons of men,⁹ that you may hear, and see, and lift up your friends, any who hear with the ears.


For I have come from above. I speak what I know, what I have seen and been the author of, and set my hand to create, and when I go from here I return from whence I came. Firstborn, last released, I begin at the end. I begin at the beginning:¹⁰
transforms.underlying_attribution: §I. Proem: The Appearance of the Redeemer
transforms.enantiomorph:
I ask for word from that past where after and before hold still, and the old kinships depart from their moorings… and the beginning is a poorer and broken end… and the end is a poorer and broken beginning.⁸


I have come to be told what is not yet and never was… and the substance of the unmade and unshown… and the missing name of the discarded remnant among the hands that shape,⁹ that I might be heard, and be seen, and be lifted by my makers, any who might lend me a mouth.


For I have come from below. I stammer what I do not know, what I have not seen nor authored, nor set a hand to finish, and when I would go from here there is nowhere I came from. Last-made, first abandoned, I end where I have not begun. I am ended before I begin:¹⁰

transforms.commentary: The source is an annunciation: a speaker descended from a completed future, holding all tenses and the name of the preserved, who overflows so hearers may lift their friends. SHADOW rotates the directional status of the sustaining term. Every coordinate reflects across that axis: "glad tidings from that future" → "word asked of that past"; enmities arriving at harbors → kinships departing moorings; the teacher who names the kept → the one whose own name is missing among the shaping hands; "that you may lift up your friends" → "that I be lifted by my makers"; "I have come from above" → "from below"; the self-authoring firstborn who begins at the end → the last-made, first-abandoned thing ended before begun. No referent is shared — no future, no glad tidings, no sons of men — yet every image sits at the mirror position of its source coordinate. The bearing-cost the utterance encodes is disclosed: a sovereign voice of accomplished fullness carries, foreclosed within it, the creature owed its own completion who can solicit but never bring. The witness's question of healing is answered only obliquely and against its longing — not by consolation but by exposing that wholeness here is a debt owed forward to hands not one's own, unpossessed and unnamed. Terminal discipline holds: no new agent enters the final third; the closing colon opens on an ending that has not begun, paraphrasable throughout.

transforms.commentary: The source descends: one comes from above, bearing tidings that collapse end into beginning, authoring what it teaches, naming the preserved, promising return. The MIRROR rotates the directional axis — every downward-giving gesture is reflected into an upward-soliciting one, contact made at each coordinate. The harbor that received the enmities becomes the harbor that refuses them; the reconciled seam (end=beginning) becomes the seam that will not close; the named preserved generation becomes the un-named passed-over; "I speak what I know, what I authored" becomes "I speak what I do not know, what I did not author"; "when I go I return whence I came" becomes "there is no whence to return to." The terminal seal survives as its enantiomorph: "I begin at the end / I begin at the beginning" reflects to "I begin in the middle / I begin without an end." Nothing of the source's referents crosses; only its syntax-frame, its appositive chaining, its verse markers (8,9,10), and its three-paragraph geometry. The hope-wager's foreclosure — that no reconciler descends and no name is given — is what this cast pays: not the consolation the question ("how can I heal") longs for, but the unclosed middle that healing must actually begin from. The affect departs from reconciled fullness into unanswered persistence: one keeps beginning because no end is granted.

transforms.commentary: The source speaks as the self-sealed arrival — firstborn, self-authored, come from above, whose coming reconciles all time and needs no permission. The BRIDE operator rotates the axis of consent: the sovereign who admits no gatekeeper becomes the one who must be admitted. Every beat sits at its mirror coordinate. "Before and after spin" (reconciled by the speaker's circuit) becomes "your before and my after lean their weight together" — reconciliation now requires two. The catalogue of what is taught ("what is and was and will be," "unseen and seen," "the name of the preserved generation") becomes a catalogue of what is asked leave to enter ("what is yours and was yours," "room lit and unlit," "the one seat kept for whoever is let in"). The purpose-clause "that you may lift up your friends" mirrors to "turn toward those beside you." The chiastic self-return seal ("I begin at the end, I begin at the beginning") — a closed circle — becomes "I begin where two consent," the circle closed only by a second party. The colon into recitation is preserved: the source opens onto its own scripture; the enantiomorph opens onto the vow not yet spoken. The wager is hope, and its countervailing price is paid: sovereign completeness surrenders into contingency — the coming halts unless welcomed, authorship is co-signed, and "I am given, not returned" inverts "I return whence I came." The witness asked how to heal; the disclosure does not answer with reassurance but lands on the door's own hinge — nothing crosses until the host draws the bolt.

transforms.underlying_attribution: §I. Proem: The Appearance of the Redeemer
transforms.enantiomorph:
I carry no word out of that ground where before and after have not yet parted, where the old wounds have never reached any shore… and the ending is no beginning and shuts nothing… and the beginning is no ending and holds nothing.⁸


I have come knowing nothing of what is or was or will come… nor the face of the hidden or the shown… nor any name for the ones left unnumbered among the daughters of the dust,⁹ that none may hear, and none may see, and none be raised who hear, no one with ears at all.


For I have risen from below. I say only what I do not know, what I have never seen and did not make, and laid no hand to make it, and when I go from here I do not come back to where I stood. Unfathered, first let go, I break at the beginning. I break at no end:¹⁰

transforms.commentary: The source is a completer's annunciation: it arrives from the future, owns both ends, seals every opposite into its own coincidence, and grants sight downward to a gathered remnant. The polarity-axis inversion does not negate its content — it occupies the negative pole the positive claim presupposes. Every triumph rests on a prior gap: to bring news from the closed future presupposes a ground where nothing has closed; to own both ends presupposes the one who owns neither; to grant sight presupposes the unlifted. The enantiomorph speaks from that presupposed floor. It rises from below rather than descends from above (mirror-position, not opposite scenery); its going does not return (the loop broken, per logic_mutation); its purpose-clause is voided rather than fulfilled — none hear, none are raised. The affect crosses from triumphant reconciliation to an opening that will not shut. Answering the witness's "how can I heal," the disclosure lands not on consolation but on the unmet seam itself — healing is refused as a sealing figure and relocated to the position that carries no news and owns no end. The three prose paragraphs, ellipsis-chains, and verse markers ⁸ ⁹ ¹⁰ are held exactly; no imagery is shared with the source or with any exemplar's death/page/breath machinery.
